newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Kok sees no risk of weak euro if EMU criteria met.
newsitem.headline: Kok sees no risk of weak euro if EMU criteria met.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Friday he saw no reason for a single European currency to be weaker than the currencies of participant member countries if the criteria for economic and monetary union are met.

"So if, and that is the set of instruments of Maastricht, if the participants in the Euro from 1999 on really fulfill the criteria there is no risk or danger at all that the strength of that new currency Euro will be less than the strength of the currencies in the individual participants," Kok said in an interview with business broadcaster CNBC.

Kok, whose country holds the current EU presidency until after the Amsterdam summit in June, acknowledged nervousness about switching a national currency for the euro but said negotiations early in 1998 should bring clarity.

"People are unsure what the future will bring and I think there will be more clarity about that by the beginning of next year when we will have arbitrations on the question of who participates. But the basis for continuing with the single currency is still there," Kok said.
